question.text: Kanchenjunga Credit Fund (Cat II) has completed its original 7-year tenure and 2-year extension. No further extension has been voted. What is the maximum period within which the AIF must fully liquidate, and what is the threshold for any extension?

answer.text: Must liquidate within 3 months; no further extension permitted
Must fully liquidate within 1 YEAR following expiration of tenure (original or extended) in absence of 2/3 unit-holder consent
May extend indefinitely with Sponsor's approval
Must liquidate immediately on tenure end

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Reg 29 and the tenure-extension framework: Extension of tenure of Cat I/II AIFs is permitted up to 2 years, with approval of 2/3 of unit-holders by value. In the ABSENCE of such consent, the AIF shall fully liquidate WITHIN 1 YEAR following expiration of the fund tenure or extended tenure. For AI-only Funds, the extension window is up to 5 YEARS (also requires 2/3 consent). The Trap: Option A (3 months) is over-aggressive. Option C is operational overreach. Option D (immediate) ignores orderly wind-up needs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests wind-up timing. LVF/AI-only extension is 5 years vs 2 years for regular Cat I/II — key differentiator. Mutual Fund wind-up timeline (V-A) is different — typically upon SEBI regulatory intervention. Manager's Pro-Tip: If heading into forced-liquidation, prepare a Liquidation-Only Period (LOP) playbook: (i) identify secondary-sale buyers for residual portfolio, (ii) pre-negotiate bulk-portfolio sale with secondary PE firms, (iii) communicate timeline clearly to LPs. Distressed liquidation routinely yields 60-70% of reasonable-exit NAV — haircut is severe.
